- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is positive (especially >0.3), especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or low (especially <0.2) and price is trending downward.
- Correct for lagged mean reversion: if true price drops sharply after a forecast peak, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next period.
- Avoid overshoot after sentiment spikes: if sentiment rises sharply and forecast jumps, cap forecast at 10–15% below prior peak.
- Weight recent sentiment more heavily in short-term (1–3 day) forecasts; use sentiment average over 5–7 days for longer horizons.
- If true price falls below 70% of recent 10-day average, reduce forecast by 10–20% to avoid overconfidence in downward momentum.
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.25 or more), apply smoothing: forecast = weighted average of 3–5 prior values + sentiment-adjusted drift.
